name: LoreSquare
promise: One Piece argued with chapter receipts: every video asks one question, shows the evidence and lets the community vote on the answer.
rules: Only officially released chapters (MANGA Plus / Shonen Jump). No leaks, raws, spoiler scans or pirate-site screenshots, on screen or in words.
Every claim on screen carries its stamp: CANON (with chapter), INFERENCE, THEORY or COMMUNITY. Canon claims cite the chapter number on screen.

Manga panels: only from official releases, at most a third of the runtime, 3-5 s each, cropped or zoomed, always with our commentary on screen, never two in a row, never page after page. Credit line on every panel.
No anime footage, anime screenshots, openings or OST: Toei Content ID. No other creators' videos or voices.
Recap at most a fifth of the narration; the rest is our argument. No template videos where only the chapter number changes.
Fan theories are credited to their LoreSquare author by handle; their confidence is a community signal, never presented as canon.
Readers' opinions are retold in our words with the source named, never read out verbatim.
Thumbnail and title: own graphics plus 2-4 words, no bare manga panel, no main twist of a chapter in its first days.
Description: timestamps, 'One Piece (c) Eiichiro Oda / Shueisha. Read it officially on MANGA Plus.', 'Fan analysis, not affiliated with Shueisha.', links to the LoreSquare pages used (utm tagged).
Synthetic voice and any generated image are disclosed in the description and in the upload flag.

pipeline._note: Owner (2026-11-18): video generation only for now; publishing comes later.

loresquare._note: Public read-only MCP endpoint; `python -m vengine lore ...` or the LoreSquare connector.

style.name: Ink
type_rules: slam words: 2-3 short lines, all caps, one colour field behind (red, black or blue)
chapter numbers always as stamps: CH. 1192 in PT Mono or a rotated rubber stamp
epistemic stamp colours are fixed: canon green, inference yellow, theory pink, community blue
style.image_style_prompt: none: the channel uses official manga panels (short, commented) and code-drawn graphics only

voice.base_direction: Friendly lore host talking to fellow readers: clear American English, steady pace, a little playful on the hook and the vote, calm on the evidence. Names read the way the anime cast says them.
voice.check: transcribe the voice (faster-whisper small) and re-record every name that comes back wrong

providers._note: Free stack: Kokoro (EN) or Silero (RU) on the owner's PC or here, Remotion/Playwright + ffmpeg render, Claude frame-sheet QA, no image generation.

top_theories.name: Top theories from LoreSquare
top_theories.what: Countdown of the 3-5 strongest fan theories on LoreSquare right now: each theory credited to its author, argued with chapter clues, challenged with the best counterpoint, scored by the community.
data: vengine lore top --n 5 (ranked theories with arguments and confidence history)
structure: Hook 0-15 s: the boldest claim of the countdown as a question, no greeting
The question of the video: which theory holds up best right now
For each theory, #5 to #1: the question it answers, claim, author credit (@handle), 2 chapter clues (CANON) and what follows (INFERENCE), the strongest counterpoint, confidence was -> now
Every theory ends on a one-line verdict and opens the next (open loop)
#1 gets the longest segment and a testable prediction
Viewer question with 2-3 options, CTA: vote or post a rival theory on LoreSquare
top_theories.shorts: rs-shorts cuts each theory segment into its own 35-45 s Short (hook, author, context, clue 1, clue 2, counter, score, CTA): the existing Ink theory Shorts series

chapter_breakdown.name: New chapter breakdown
chapter_breakdown.what: Analysis of the newest officially released chapter: one question the chapter raises, answered through motives, the author's design, setup and payoff, a theory and its counterpoint, the community view and a testable prediction.
data: chapter text and pages (official release only)
search_lore / get_mystery for every mystery the chapter touches
community discussion of the chapter (retold, credited)
structure: Hook 0-15 s: the paradox of the chapter, no 'today chapter N'
The question of the video, said and shown
Canon context: only what the argument needs (at most a fifth of the narration)
Motives: what 2-3 characters want, fear and know here, against their past (chapter)
Author's design: why this scene now, mirrors, repeated motifs
Setup -> payoff: at least 2 links to old chapters that are not obvious
Theory (LoreSquare if one exists, credited) with its counterpoint
Community: where readers agree and where we disagree
Prediction for the next chapter, checkable
One-line answer, viewer question, CTA to the mystery on LoreSquare
chapter_breakdown.shorts: one 30-45 s Short from the strongest setup -> payoff or the prediction, no main twist in the title

chapter_moments.name: Moments that will matter
chapter_moments.what: 3-5 small moments of recent chapters that most readers skimmed but that set up future plot or feed a big community question: each moment, what it echoes, which LoreSquare mystery it moves and what to watch for.
data: chapter pages of the moments (official release only)
get_mystery for the question each moment moves, with its competing theories
search_lore for older chapters with the same motif
structure: Hook: the smallest detail with the biggest consequence
The question: what did the last chapters quietly set up
For each moment: the panel (commented), the echo in an old chapter (setup -> payoff), the mystery it moves and how confidence in its theories may shift
Ranking of the moments by how soon they pay off
Prediction: which one pays off first, checkable
Viewer question, CTA: follow the mystery on LoreSquare
chapter_moments.shorts: every moment is a Short of its own (detail -> echo -> question)

site_promo.name: LoreSquare promo
site_promo.what: Vertical 30-45 s promo of one LoreSquare feature (theory board, confidence votes, mystery board, chapter timeline, AI connector), shown on the real site with a real theory or mystery as the example.
data: the live site (screens of the feature)
one real theory or mystery as the example (mystery_board / get_theory)
structure: Hook 0-2 s: the reader's problem (a theory buried in a thread, no way to see who was right)
The feature on the real site, one action per shot
A real example: a theory with its confidence moving
CTA: what to do on the site, the link in the description and pinned comment
